title: Clinical comparison between isolated cartilage therapy and combined procedure of hindfoot correction in osteochondrosis dissecans tali
summary:
For the treatment of osteochondrosis dissecans (OD) tali, the death of certain areas of cartilage and bone at the ankle joint, different treatment methods or surgical methods are available (also depending on the stage of the disease). In the first method, the disease is treated by cartilage therapy, and in the second method, an additional correction is performed on the hindfoot in addition to cartilage therapy.
The aim of this study is to compare the results of patients who have already undergone surgery with these two methods at our clinic after at least one year, and to analyze whether one method offers an advantage.
Patients who have already had surgery will be contacted and, if they wish, invited to the clinic for a study-related follow-up appointment. At this appointment, the patient will be examined according to routine orthopedic practice and will be asked to complete the following questionnaires: EFAS (European Foot and Ankle Society) score, FAOS (Foot and Ankle Outcome Score), SF-36 (Short Form 36), UCLA (University of California Los Angeles) score.
If the patient does not have the possibility to come to the follow-up examination, he/she can also fill in the questionnaires by mail.
conditions: Osteochondrosis dissecans : ankle and foot [tarsal, metatarsal, toes, ankle, other joints of the foot].

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with a surgically repaired osteochondral lesion:
o Without hindfoot correction, as there was no deformity preoperatively.
o With hindfoot correction, which were performed additively due to malalignment
- Follow-up time: Min. 12 months postoperatively
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients under 18 years
- Wheelchair requirement
- Successful arthrodesis of the foot (excluding TMT-I arthrodesis as part of hindfoot correction)
